lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Percentage Increases and GST
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 7, Session 3
lesson.footer: Money and Percentages | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 3

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09): modelling practical situations with percentage increases, such as GST and price rises, using efficient calculation strategies
plan.shape: compare-two-models: a discount bar beside an increase bar, because the only change from Session 1 is adding instead of taking off
plan.criticalFeature: an increase is added on: find the percentage, then add it to the price
decisionPoints: the hinge: a $250 ticket goes up 20%
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation
plan.catchUp: Missed Sessions 1 or 2? Show 10% of $70 = $7 on a bar model; today we add it on instead of taking it off.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it
Under it: discount takes off, increase adds on

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. A GST table, price rises, a mistake to fix, and ticket, wage and club problems.
resources.title: Percentage Increases and GST
resources.subtitle: Find the increase, then add it on.

example.prompt: A $50 game plus 10% GST. Total price?

items.prompt: Find the GST (10%) and the price with GST.
Sort each situation: does the price go up or down?
Kai worked out a $60 jacket after a 20% price rise. Find his mistake and fix it.
A $100 skateboard rises 10%, then is 10% off. What does it cost now?
items.explain: Rise: $110. Then 10% of $110 = $11 off: $99. The second 10% is of a bigger amount.

example.prompt: Footy club fees were $120. They rise by 15%. New fee?

items.prompt: A concert ticket is $85 before a 20% booking increase. What is the new price?
Mia earns $15 an hour. She gets a 10% pay rise. How much will she earn for a 6-hour shift now?

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Two rises in a row, removing GST from a price, and a percentage change puzzle, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Rising Prices
resources.subtitle: Rises on rises. Work back from GST.

items.prompt: A $500 bike rises 10% one year and 10% the next. What does it cost after two years?
Is a 20% rise the same as two 10% rises? Explain with an example.
items.answer: No: two 10% rises give more, because the second 10% is of a bigger amount ($100 to $121, not $120).

example.prompt: A price with GST is $55. Price before GST?
steps: With GST is 110% of the price.

items.prompt: Each price includes 10% GST. Find the price before GST and the GST.

example.prompt: A $40 ticket now costs $50. What percentage increase?

items.prompt: Find two items in an old catalogue or make some up, with an old and a new price. Work out the percentage change for each and say which rose more.
items.answer: Check: increase = new - old; percentage = increase out of the old price × 100; the comparison uses percentages, not dollars.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: 10% increases only, a two-step frame, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Increases: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Step 1: find 10%. Step 2: add it on.

slides.notes: Session 3 of our money and percentages fortnight: today prices go up, with GST and price rises.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk; calculators are optional for checking. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with the four processes.
ASK: What is 4 657 plus 2 879?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7 536
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> line up the places and regroup together on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 7 536. Tick it or fix it, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, and they add that column again.
notes.prep: Review of the four processes (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is 8 003 take away 3 476?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4 527
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> regroup across the zeros together on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 4 527.
Check by adding back: 4 527 plus 3 476 is 8 003.
trap: taking the smaller digit from the bigger one.
Fix: ask if the top digit is big enough, and they regroup.
notes.prep: Four processes review: subtraction across zeros.

beats: ASK: What is 46 times 7?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 322
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> split 46 into 40 and 6, multiply each by 7. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 40 times 7 is 280 and 6 times 7 is 42: 322.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: multiplying only the ones.
Fix: split 46 into 40 and 6, and they redo it.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some short division with the division bracket.
Divide each digit from the left, and carry any remainder across.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 123
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 123.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.
notes.prep: Division fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Keep the whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1 305
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 1 305.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 5 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 6 552
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 6 552.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to work out percentage increases, including GST.
successCriteria: I can find a percentage of a price.
I can add a percentage increase to find the new price.
I can explain when a price goes up or down, and check my answer makes sense.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: So far, prices have come down in sales.
Today prices go up, with GST and price rises.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 a percentage of a price is reachable for everyone; SC2 the new price after an increase is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 up or down is the stretch.

slides.title: Off or on?
slides.prompt: What does $40 become with each sign?

beats: POINT to each sign.
SAY: Here's a 40 dollar item with two different signs.
ASK: What does 40 dollars become with 25 percent off, and with 25 percent more?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $30 and $50
SCAN boards for 30 and 50.
80%+ -> cold call one student: What stayed the same in both?
Less -> find 25 percent first, 10 dollars, then take off or add on. Re-ask.
SAY: Both times, 25 percent is 10 dollars.
Off takes it away, and more adds it on. Today, prices go up.
trap: writing $65 for 25% more.
Fix: find 25 percent of 40 first, and they redo it.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: the same percentage, added or taken away. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: Goods and Services Tax: an extra 10% added to the price of most things in Australia.

beats: POINT to the letters.
SAY: These letters are G, S, T. Say them with me: G, S, T.
SAY: GST stands for Goods and Services Tax.
In Australia, it adds 10 percent to the price of most things,
and the money goes to the government.
ASK: A $40 shirt plus GST. How much is the GST?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $4
trap: writing $44 for the GST.
Fix: ask how much is added, and they separate GST from the total.
notes.prep: GST is 10%: one bar part on top of ten.

beats: MODEL finding 10%.
SAY: A 70 dollar pair of headphones, plus GST.
10 percent of 70 is 7 dollars.
MODEL adding on.
SAY: GST is added on, so 70 plus 7 is 77 dollars.
That's a bit more than 70, so it makes sense.
ASK: What does a $90 item cost with GST?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $99
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent of 90 is 9, so 90 plus 9 is 99 dollars.
trap: taking the GST off.
Fix: say GST is added on, and they add.
notes.stretch: Find the price with GST in one step: 110% of $90.
notes.help: Fill in a price, GST, total table.
notes.prep: Find the increase, then add it on: the critical feature. SC1 and SC2.

slides.title: A price rise
steps: The club fee is $80. It rises 15%.

beats: MODEL building 15%.
SAY: The netball club fee is 80 dollars, and it's going up 15 percent.
10 percent is 8, and 5 percent is half of that, 4.
So 15 percent is 12 dollars.
MODEL adding on.
SAY: It's a rise, so I add: 80 plus 12 is 92 dollars.
ASK: A $60 ticket goes up 25 percent. What is the new price?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $75
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 25 percent of 60 is 15, so the new price is 75 dollars.
trap: adding 25 dollars.
Fix: find 25 percent first, and they redo it.

slides.title: $40 plus 10% GST
slides.prompt: What is the price with GST? Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: takes the GST off instead of adding it

beats: SAY: Is GST added on, or taken off?
ASK: What does a 40 dollar item cost with 10 percent GST?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What did C do?
Less -> find 10 percent of 40 together, then add it on. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 44 dollars. A took the GST off,
and C added 10 dollars instead of 10 percent.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: say GST is added on, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A: direction; C: percent as dollars.

slides.title: What is the new price?
slides.pivot: find the percentage first, then add it on
slides.followUp: cold call one board: How much was the increase?

items.say: 20 percent is 16 dollars: 64 if it's off, 96 if it's more.

say: Write each new price on your board.
trap: taking the increase off.
Fix: ask whether the price goes up or down, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Write the increase for each one too.
notes.help: Write the increase before the new price.
notes.prep: Guided practice: GST, a rise, a cents answer, and up or down. SC2 and SC3.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Find the increase, then add it on.
ASK: What is the new price of the
250 dollar ticket after a 20 percent rise?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $300
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> find 10 percent together, 25, then double it. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 20 percent of 250 is 50,
so the new price is 300 dollars. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing $200.
Fix: ask whether the price went up or down, and they add.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone writing $200 or $270 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Work out GST and price rises on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Does this price go up or down?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: taking an increase off.
Fix: ask up or down, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: two rises in a row, taking GST out, and percentage change.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: 10% increases only, with a two-step frame.
notes.prep: Independent practice: a GST table, up or down, a mistake and real problems. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: How much will you pay at the counter?

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: A scooter is 140 dollars before GST.
How much will you pay at the counter?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $154
RECORD who takes the GST off or adds $10.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing $126 or $150.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: GST on a new price.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner the difference between a discount and an increase.

notes.answer: open - listen for an increase is added on; a discount is taken off
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can work out a percentage increase?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with $126 on the board matters most.
ASK: How is an increase different from a discount?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: an increase is added on; a discount is taken off
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: multi-step money problems.
